title: One item tool: get, set, call
description: A plan to replace the six page tools and many Servex tools with one item tool and three verbs. Study only; waits for your yes.

add.text: **The plan in one line:** agents get one `item` tool with three verbs. `get` reads, `set` changes fields, `call` runs a method. All three work on whatever `Item.open(url)` opens: a page, a task, a session, a card. The five page tools go away, and so do the Servex tools that only read or write a record. The log format does not change, so no data moves. **Study only: nothing is built until you say yes.**

add.title: The three verbs
add.preview: get reads and never writes; set and call always write one log line.

add.title: What leaves page_tools.js: 1,881 lines down to about 250
add.preview: Most of the file is not tool code. Each part moves to the class it belongs to, in eight small merges.
add.text:
Most of `Servex/agents/page_tools.js` is not tool code. It holds jobs that belong to classes, so each one moves to its class. What stays is a small `ItemTool` that opens the item and calls the verb.

| Part today | Lines | Moves to |
|---|---|---|
| The core call, `run_item_now` | ~250 | `ItemTool.get / set / call`, ~80 lines |
| Turning a url into a file (`resolve`, `session_file`, `card_at`) | ~170 | a new `ItemUrl` class, reusing `Ref.file_of` |
| Moving tasks and making folders (`move_item`, `give_folder`, …) | ~270 | a new `TaskMoves` class |
| Session counts and costs (`session_state`, `nest_agents`, …) | ~170 | the `Session` class |
| Refusing a bad line (`validate`, `page_refusal`, …) | ~100 | each class's own `refuse(line)` |
| The help text (`instructions_for`, `surface_of`, …) | ~130 | a new `ItemHelp` class |
| Page text for `page_read` (`render_markdown`, …) | ~70 | `Page.as_markdown()` |
| Walking a dotted path (`walk`, `walk_queries`, …) | ~120 | `Item.get`, which already exists |
| The five page tools and an old replay | ~170 | deleted |

**Eight merges, each with its test:**
1. Add `get`, `set` and `call` beside today's `delta` and `read`, so nothing breaks. *Test:* `item_tool.test.mjs` runs each verb on a scratch session.
2. The page writes its own text. *Test:* `Page.as_markdown()` gives exactly what `page_read` gives today, on three real pages.
3. `ItemUrl`. *Test:* every url shape in `page_tools.test.mjs` resolves to the same file.
4. Each class refuses its own bad lines. *Test:* every refusal case in `page_tools.test.mjs` still refuses, with the same reason.
5. `TaskMoves`. page_tools.js re-exports it, and a script rewrites the imports (dry run first). *Test:* the existing move tests.
6. `Session.state()`. *Test:* the `session_state` cases.
7. Switch the docs, skills and voice text to the verbs (next card).
8. Remove the five page tools once a week of tool-call logs shows nobody calls them. *Test:* their alias tests go, and `item_tool.test.mjs` covers the same calls.

**Cost guess:** about $45 (eight Sonnet builds at $3–6 each, plus reviews).

add.title: Risks, and the order to switch
add.preview: Agents learn the tools from about 100 docs and the voice instructions. Add the verbs first, switch the words, remove the old tools last.
add.text:
**What could break**
- **Agents' prompts.** Agents learn the page tools from what they read. `page_set` is named in 114 docs, skills and role texts, `page_add` in 99, `page_read` in 68. If a tool goes before its docs change, agents call a tool that is not there.
- **The voice instructions.** The cloud voice app is told to use `page_set` and `page_add` for `/live/` (`Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js`, lines 25–27). If that changes during a call, the voice app's next turn fails.
- **RemoteMCP.** The cloud door forwards a chosen list of tools. A tool removed locally but still on that list fails there.
- **Servex restarts.** A tool change goes live only after a restart, and voice-app picks the time.

**The order to switch**
1. Add the three verbs beside `delta` and `read`. Nothing breaks.
2. Teach the verbs first: `core/Page/doc/ai-api.md`, the `page` skill, the role texts and the voice instructions. A script makes the edits, with a dry run first.
3. Keep the five page tools for one week. Each one's description says "use item" at the top.
4. A script counts calls to the old tools in that week's session transcripts. At zero, the tools go. Anything still calling one is fixed first.
5. RemoteMCP's list changes last, between calls.

**What does not change:** the log lines on disk, every page, and the browser.

risks.text:
**What could break**
- **Agents' prompts.** Agents learn the page tools from what they read. `page_set` is named in 114 docs, skills and role texts, `page_add` in 99, `page_read` in 68. If a tool goes before its docs change, agents call a tool that is not there.

- **RemoteMCP.** The cloud door shows the same tool list as Servex, plus its own four tools (`ask_mastermind` and three more; `RemoteMCP.tools()`, line 168). So a removed tool disappears there too, at the next restart. The voice app keeps the list it loaded until it reconnects.
- **Servex restarts.** A tool change goes live only after a restart, and voice-app picks the time.

**The order to switch**
1. Add the three verbs beside `delta` and `read`. Nothing breaks.
2. Teach the verbs first: `core/Page/doc/ai-api.md`, the `page` skill, the role texts and the voice instructions. A script makes the edits, with a dry run first.
3. Keep the five page tools for one week. Each one's description says "use item" at the top.
4. A script counts calls to the old tools in that week's session transcripts. At zero, the tools go. Anything still calling one is fixed first.
5. Remove the old tools with a restart between voice calls.

**What does not change:** the log lines on disk, every page, and the browser.

add.title: Choices made, and the alternatives
add.preview: One tool with three verbs; computed values are a get; delta stays only while the switch runs.
add.text:
- **One tool with three verbs** (chosen, your words). *Alternative:* three tools, `item_get`, `item_set` and `item_call`. Each would be simpler to describe, but agents would learn three names instead of one. It wins only if agents keep mixing up the verbs.
- **A computed value is a `get`** (chosen). The rule is easy to remember: `get` never writes, and `set` and `call` always write. *Alternative:* a computed value is a `call` that writes nothing. That matches how the class code works, but then you can't tell from the verb whether something gets written.
- **`delta` stays only while the switch runs** (chosen). It goes when the old tools go. *Alternative:* keep `delta` as a fourth, raw verb for several changes in one line. Useful, but it brings back the mixed-up shape you asked to get rid of. It wins if agents often need two changes to land together as one line.
- **The log format does not change** (chosen). *Alternative:* write the verb into the line (`{"call":"tasks.add",…}`). That would be clearer to read, but every replay and every page would have to change, and old logs would need converting.

add.title: What was already decided
add.preview: One tool taking deltas was your call on 10-12; the plan keeps one tool and splits the delta into three verbs.
add.text:
A Haiku search of the docs and session logs ([answer](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-page-design/item-three-verbs/search/answer.md), $0.37):

- **One write tool, not one per verb** (you, 2026-10-12: "a few universal tools that take deltas"; [ai-api.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/ai-api.md), "Decisions"). The old page tools were kept only as aliases so nothing broke. **This plan keeps one tool** and splits its delta into three plain verbs.
- **The page tools were built** on 2026-10-02 (`page_add`, `page_set`, `page_log`, `page_read`), then `item` beside them.
- **One tool list for local and cloud** (2026-10-15, `Servex/ext/remote/doc/mcp-unify.md`). The cloud door serves the same registry, so cutting a tool cuts it in both places.
- **Queries write nothing** (`{"summary":{}}`, `{"completion":{}}`; ai-api.md, "Asking without writing"). Under the new verbs, these become `get`.
- **Logging a computed value** (you, 2026-11-06; [core/Session/readme.md](/framework/core/Session/readme.md)): a `measured` reading that replay skips. Not built. The verbs card gives it a home: `call: "measure"`.
- **Nothing found** on three verbs or `get / set / call` before this ask: it is new.

add.title: Every Servex tool: 108, about half fold into item
add.preview: 56 read or write a record (fold into item), 50 act on processes or files (keep), 2 drop.
add.text:
A Sonnet minion counted every tool by script and checked the count against a live agent's own list: 108 tools, none missing ([the full table](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-page-design/item-three-verbs/inventory-run/table.md), $1.96).

| Mark | Count | What they are |
|---|---|---|
| **Fold into item** | 56 | They read or write a record that `Item.open(url)` can open: pages, cards, tasks, sessions, inboxes, logs |
| **Keep** | 50 | They act on the machine: agents, servers, worktrees, files, the shell, usage, wake-ups |
| **Drop** | 2 | `readme_modules` (the same code as `load_module`) and `ask_mastermind` (marked deprecated on 11-06) |

**The first wave, the plain cases** (each is one `get`, `set` or `call`):

```js
item({ path, get: "text" })                        // read_page, page_read
item({ path, call: "content.add", args: card })    // page_add, add_item
item({ path: card, set: { status: "done" } })      // card_set
item({ path: task, call: "complete", args: {…} }) // close_task
item({ path: task, set: { priority: 2 } })         // reprioritise_task
item({ path, call: "log.add", args: { msg } })     // dir_log, append_log, session_line
```

**My check on the minion's marks (a guess until each is built):** about a dozen of the 56 also *do* something besides writing a record. `say` and `updates` talk to a live voice seat, `quick_fix` and `kill_task` start or stop work, and `create_card` tells the owner. Those stay as their own tools for now, and fold only if their side effect can move into the class's own method. That leaves about 40 to fold.

A Sonnet minion counted every tool by script and checked the count against a live agent's own list: 108 tools, none missing ([the full table](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-page-design/item-three-verbs/inventory-run/table.md), $1.96).

| Mark | Count | What they are |
|---|---|---|
| **Fold into item** | 56 | They read or write a record that `Item.open(url)` can open: pages, cards, tasks, sessions, inboxes, logs |
| **Keep** | 50 | They act on the machine: agents, servers, worktrees, files, the shell, usage, wake-ups |
| **Drop** | 2 | `readme_modules` (the same code as `load_module`) and `ask_mastermind` (marked deprecated on 11-06) |

**The first wave, the plain cases** (each is one `get`, `set` or `call`):

```js

item({ path, call: "content.add", args: card })    // page_add, add_item
item({ path: card, set: { status: "done" } })      // card_set
item({ path: session, set: { title: "…" } })      // rename_session
item({ path: task, set: { priority: 2 } })         // reprioritise_task
item({ path, call: "log.add", args: { msg } })     // dir_log, append_log, session_line
```

**My check on the minion's marks (a guess until each is built):** about a dozen of the 56 also *do* something besides writing a record. `say` and `updates` talk to a live voice seat, `quick_fix` and `kill_task` start or stop work, `close_task` stops the task's servers and worktrees, and `create_card` tells the owner. Those stay as their own tools for now, and fold only if their side effect can move into the class's own method. That leaves about 40 to fold.
